description: Manage registration and subscription to the Red Hat Subscription Management entitlement platform using the subscription-manager command, registering using D-Bus if possible.

parameters.name: activationkey
parameters.description: Supply an activation key for use with registration.

parameters.name: auto_attach
parameters.description: Upon successful registration, auto-consume available subscriptions. Please note that the alias autosubscribe was removed in community.general 9.0.0. Choices: false true

parameters.name: consumer_id
parameters.description: References an existing consumer ID to resume using a previous registration for this system. If the system’s identity certificate is lost or corrupted, this option allows it to resume using its previous identity and subscriptions. The default is to not specify a consumer ID so a new ID is created.

parameters.name: consumer_name
parameters.description: Name of the system to register, defaults to the hostname.

parameters.name: consumer_type
parameters.description: The type of unit to register, defaults to system.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: Register with a specific environment in the destination org. Used with Red Hat Satellite or Katello.

parameters.name: force_register
parameters.description: Register the system even if it is already registered. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Organization ID to use in conjunction with activationkey.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Access.redhat.com or Red Hat Satellite or Katello password.

parameters.name: pool_ids
parameters.description: Specify subscription pool IDs to consume. A pool ID may be specified as a string - just the pool ID (for example 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef), or as a dict with the pool ID as the key, and a quantity as the value (for example 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef: 2. If the quantity is provided, it is used to consume multiple entitlements from a pool (the pool must support this). Default: []

parameters.name: release
parameters.description: Set a release version.

parameters.name: rhsm_baseurl
parameters.description: Specify CDN baseurl.

parameters.name: rhsm_repo_ca_cert
parameters.description: Specify an alternative location for a CA certificate for CDN.

parameters.name: server_hostname
parameters.description: Specify an alternative Red Hat Subscription Management or Red Hat Satellite or Katello server.

parameters.name: server_insecure
parameters.description: Enable or disable https server certificate verification when connecting to server_hostname.

parameters.name: server_port
parameters.description: Specify the port when registering to the Red Hat Subscription Management or Red Hat Satellite or Katello server.

parameters.name: server_prefix
parameters.description: Specify the prefix when registering to the Red Hat Subscription Management or Red Hat Satellite or Katello server.

parameters.name: server_proxy_hostname
parameters.description: Specify an HTTP proxy hostname.

parameters.name: server_proxy_password
parameters.description: Specify a password for HTTP proxy with basic authentication.

parameters.name: server_proxy_port
parameters.description: Specify an HTTP proxy port.

parameters.name: server_proxy_scheme
parameters.description: Specify an HTTP proxy scheme, for example http or https.

parameters.name: server_proxy_user
parameters.description: Specify a user for HTTP proxy with basic authentication.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Whether to register and subscribe (present), or unregister (absent) a system. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: syspurpose
parameters.description: Set syspurpose attributes in file /etc/rhsm/syspurpose/syspurpose.json and synchronize these attributes with RHSM server. Syspurpose attributes help attach the most appropriate subscriptions to the system automatically. When syspurpose.json file already contains some attributes, then new attributes overwrite existing attributes. When some attribute is not listed in the new list of attributes, the existing attribute is removed from syspurpose.json file. Unknown attributes are ignored.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Sso.redhat.com API access token.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Access.redhat.com or Red Hat Satellite or Katello username.

examples:
- name: Register as user (joe_user) with password (somepass) and auto-subscribe to available content.
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    auto_attach: true

- name: Same as above but subscribe to a specific pool by ID.
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    pool_ids: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

- name: Register and subscribe to multiple pools.
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    pool_ids:
      - 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
      - 1123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

- name: Same as above but consume multiple entitlements.
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    pool_ids:
      - 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef: 2
      - 1123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef: 4

- name: Register and pull existing system data.
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    consumer_id: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

- name: Register as user credentials into given environment (against Red Hat Satellite or Katello), and auto-subscribe.
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    environment: Library
    auto_attach: true

- name: Register as user (joe_user) with password (somepass) and a specific release
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    release: 7.4

- name: Register as user (joe_user) with password (somepass), set syspurpose attributes and synchronize them with server
  community.general.redhat_subscription:
    state: present
    username: joe_user
    password: somepass
    auto_attach: true
    syspurpose:
      usage: "Production"
      role: "Red Hat Enterprise Server"
      service_level_agreement: "Premium"
      addons:
        - addon1
        - addon2
      sync: true

return_values.name: subscribed_pool_ids
return_values.description: List of pool IDs to which system is now subscribed. Returned: success Sample: {"8a85f9815ab905d3015ab928c7005de4": "1"}
